articles.title: The kindness of strangers: After my wife died, a football club made an extraordinary gesture
articles.summary: My son had only played two seasons for St Mary’s Greensborough, five years earlier. I don’t know how they even got our new address but they took the time to send him a care package. Footy clubs, and the AFL specifically, have a lot to answer for in terms of sexism.
body: When we lived in Melbourne many years ago, my son played a couple of seasons for St Mary’s Greensborough. Unfortunately for him, I secured a job in central Queensland and moved the family north.

During our new adventure, my wife was diagnosed with breast cancer. It was stage four, so she was in trouble straight away. She battled it fiercely but died in 2015, about five years after we left Melbourne.

As my children and I began to emerge from the fog of grief, a package arrived in the mail for my son. Inside was a St Mary’s Greensborough football jersey with our surname emblazoned across the back. Attached was a note that read: “Thinking of you after the loss of your mum.”
The support around us as a family when my wife was sick, and when she died, was fantastic. I am so grateful for that. But sometimes it’s the gestures that come out of left field that really move you.
points: My son had only played two seasons for St Mary’s Greensborough, five years earlier.
I don’t know how they even got our new address but they took the time to send him a care package.
Footy clubs, and the AFL specifically, have a lot to answer for in terms of sexism.

articles.title: Forget the seven-year itch: opposite-sex marriages more likely to end after two decades
articles.summary: ONS data for England and Wales shows 26% of heterosexual divorces in 2025 followed 20 years or more of marriage. Most couples are aware of the dreaded “seven-year itch”, when the honeymoon period wears off and real life starts to bite.
body: Now official data has shown that couples in England and Wales are more likely to split after 20 years. According to Office for National Statistics figures, more than a quarter of all divorces between opposite-sex couples happened after 20 years or longer of marriage.

The former Strictly presenter Tess Daly recently separated from her husband, the presenter Vernon Kay, after 22 years of marriage. The Downton Abbey actor Hugh Bonneville split from his wife, Lulu Williams, in 2023 after 25 years, and in 2019, Colin Firth announced his separation from wife, Livia Giuggioli, after 22. Last year, the Hollywood actor Nicole Kidman and singer Keith Urban separated after almost 20 years of marriage.

Divorce lawyers have previously said some couples are putting off splitting up because of the cost of living crisis. Recent figures have shown the average length of a marriage ending in divorce in England and Wales reached a record high last year.

ONS figures have long appeared to show that the seven-year itch exists; since records began in 1963, the largest proportion of divorces each year has almost always been among those who have spent between five and nine years as a couple.
points: ONS data for England and Wales shows 26% of heterosexual divorces in 2025 followed 20 years or more of marriage.

articles.title: Great Pottery Throw Down judge Keith Brymer Jones looks back: ‘Men like seeing me be emotional’
articles.summary: The potter and presenter on a tricky childhood, his religious calling for clay, and cross-dressing as Adele. Born in London in 1965, Keith Brymer Jones is a potter, ceramic designer and TV judge.
body: This photo was taken in our family home in Finchley. Socks, shorts and a T-shirt was my usual outfit for scabbing around in the garden aged 11. I was a complete and utter square.

My main passion at this time was dancing – ballet, tap and Highland and Scottish country dancing. But I was starting to realise I should stop telling people about it. I was about to embark on my first year of secondary school at St Mary’s in Hendon and knew I’d get stick for it.

I kept it under wraps, but I was bullied for three years. It was the start of a difficult part of my life, especially after my grandfather died. His death happened in front of me, when he fell down the stairs while having a heart attack. Unsurprisingly, my OCD developed around this time; I used it to try to create a sense of control and order. Everything around me had to be at 90 degrees – pens, pencils and the curtains. My bedroom began to resemble an empty studio, because it was easier than having belongings. To this day, I do like a tidy workshop.
points: The potter and presenter on a tricky childhood, his religious calling for clay, and cross-dressing as Adele.

articles.title: Exclusive: Inside the Academy Museum Gala, Where Hollywood Let Its Hair Down
articles.summary: Hollywood turned out in full force on Saturday for its favorite Q4 night out: the sixth annual Academy Museum of Motion Pictures gala, an evening that doubled as a celebration of the museum’s anniversary and raised more than $14 million for its exhibitions, education initiatives, and public…
body: Co-chaired by Tom Ford, Robert Rodriguez, Steven Spielberg, and Kate Capshaw, and presented in partnership with Rolex, the night once again drew a guest list that read like a year’s worth of premieres rolled into one.

Ana de Armas, Jacob Elordi, Sabrina Carpenter, and Colin Farrell were among the arrivals, while Kendall Jenner, Hailey Bieber, and a vintage Balenciaga-clad Kim Kardashian were giddy in a corner together. Sarah Paulson, in custom Ferragamo, had designer Maximilian Davis on her arm. Old Hollywood and new-gen stars alike were well represented, as the likes of Hunter Schafer, Rosé, and Connor Storrie made the rounds with Pamela Anderson and Pierce Brosnan.

Amy Homma, director and president of the Academy Museum and Academy Collection, opened the program with a look back at the museum’s first five years, followed by a toast from trustee Olivier de Givenchy. Jamie Lee Curtis, no stranger to a scream, then took the stage to reflect on the enduring pull of the horror genre and spotlight the museum’s newest exhibition, The Horror Show. Fittingly, she introduced Rodriguez, who presented filmmaker and composer John Carpenter, the man behind Halloween, with the Luminary Award.

articles.title: The Next Generation of Collagen Is Here—Does It Work?
articles.summary: Collagen supplements can help with healthier joints and smoother skin—but does the latest version live up to the hype?
body: A new generation of collagen supplements is here: Collagen tripeptides are the smallest version of collagen possible and said to be more easily absorbed by the body and more effective at stimulating the body’s own collagen production—but is that the case?

I may have had unrealistic expectations when I first tried with collagen supplements. After taking them for months, I expected to look 10 years younger when I looked in the mirror. To say I was disappointed was an understatement. I experimented with different formulas— marine collagen, bovine collagen, collagen peptides, collagen powder, capsules, gels, and even gummies—but I still wasn’t convinced. The results were yet to live up to the promises.
points: Collagen supplements can help with healthier joints and smoother skin—but does the latest version live up to the hype?

articles.title: Tommy’s Take on Why More Is More When it Comes to Accessorizing
articles.summary: In monthly installments surrounding a fashion theme, street style photographer Tommy Ton gives us an unfiltered close-up of the outfits that caught his eye and why.
body: Is more more, or is less more? For years, we’ve been told that good taste is knowing when to stop. Coco Chanel’s famous advice of looking in the mirror before leaving the house and removing one thing has become something of a fashion commandment for many. But I’ve always wondered what happens when we do the opposite. What if, instead of taking something away, you add another necklace, another ring, another earring, another bracelet? What if the most interesting thing about getting dressed is not knowing when to stop, but having the confidence not to?

After seasons of quiet luxury and wardrobes edited down to the essentials, I find myself drawn to a more expressive approach to accessorizing. Somewhere along the way, restraint became synonymous with sophistication, and the absence of adornment was elevated into a marker of taste. But minimalism, for all its elegance, can become its own uniform. When everyone is wearing the same monogram pendant or oversized belt buckle, how much individuality is left?
points: In monthly installments surrounding a fashion theme, street style photographer Tommy Ton gives us an unfiltered close-up of the outfits that caught his eye and why.

articles.title: 23 Most Comfortable Walking Shoes for Travel: Sneakers, Sandals, Boots, and More
articles.summary: Editor-tested sneakers, boots, and sandals for all-day support.
body: In everyday life, I'm a shoe girl. My closet is filled with more sneakers, flats, sandals, heels, boots, flip-flops, and clogs than I need. It's a bit excessive, sure, but I like having options! When packing for a trip, I really have to rein myself in, particularly when I'm only bringing a carry-on. With room for just a few pairs of shoes, versatility is key, but of course, comfort is what really reigns supreme. Comfortable walking shoes are crucial to any vacation, whether your walking plans involve an all-day hike, a stroll around a new city center, or just a few laps around the pool deck.

As such, my fellow Condé Nast Traveler editors and I are constantly on the lookout for truly comfortable, walk-all-day shoes to wear on our travels. The best walking shoes leave you blister-free, with no irritated heels or sore arches. They've got to be well-cushioned, and ideally, don't require much break-in time, though we will make exceptions for long-lasting pairs like hiking boots or leather sandals that need some more TLC at the start.
points: Editor-tested sneakers, boots, and sandals for all-day support.
